---
title: "Sources"
description: "Every vendor Storywell can read from, how to produce its input, and which services aren't supported yet — and why."
---

A **source** is a vendor Storywell can read finished books from. Each source owns its own
auth/fetch details and normalises everything into the same internal shape, so the StoryGraph
matching-and-writing side is identical regardless of where the books came from.

Three things vary per source and matter for results:

- **ISBNs.** Sources that export ISBNs (Goodreads, Kobo, LibraryThing, Hardcover, Literal, Calibre,
  Bookwyrm) let StoryGraph match by identifier, which is far more reliable than fuzzy title/author
  matching (Audible, Apple Books, and Kindle have none).
- **Media format.** An `audio` source marks the audiobook edition on StoryGraph; `ebook`/`print`
  sources tag the best-matching edition; `mixed` is left to per-book resolution.
- **Read signal.** Most sources prove a book was *finished* and route it to your **read** shelf.
  Catalogue and borrow sources (LibraryThing, Libby) carry no finished signal — they only sync when
  you opt them onto a shelf with `--shelf` (see [shelf routing](#shelf-routing)).

## At a glance

| Source | Format | Where the data comes from | Read signal | Key flags |
|--------|--------|---------------------------|-------------|-----------|
| `audible` | audio | `audible-cli` registration | progress vs. threshold | `--auth-file`, `--profile` |
| `goodreads` | mixed | Settings → Export CSV | `read` shelf | `--file` |
| `kobo` | ebook | on-device `KoboReader.sqlite` | read status | `--file` |
| `literal` | mixed | GraphQL token (login) | `FINISHED` status | `--token` |
| `applebooks` | ebook | on-device `BKLibrary*.sqlite` (macOS) | finished flag + progress | `--file` (auto-detected) |
| `calibre` | mixed | local `metadata.db` | custom read column | `--file`, `--read-column` |
| `bookwyrm` | mixed | Settings → Export CSV | `shelf` column | `--file` |
| `librarything` | mixed | CSV/JSON export | none (catalogue) | `--file`, `--shelf`, `--read-date`, `--collection` |
| `libby` | mixed | Libby Timeline / OverDrive history CSV | none (borrow) | `--file`, `--shelf` |
| `kindle` | ebook | Amazon "Request My Data" CSVs | inferred from sessions | `--file` |
| `hardcover` | mixed | GraphQL token | read status | `--token` |

## Stable sources

These are validated against real exports and are the safest to run unattended.

### Audible

- **Format:** audio · **Flags:** `--auth-file`, `--profile`

Reads your finished audiobooks through the maintained
[`audible`](https://github.com/mkb79/Audible) library. Set it up once with `audible-cli`
(see [Install → Audible](install.qmd#audible)). Audible has no public API and no ISBNs, so matching
is title/author based.

```sh
storywell sync --source audible
```

### Goodreads

- **Format:** mixed · **Flags:** `--file`

Export your library from Goodreads under **Settings → Export**, which produces a
`goodreads_library_export.csv`. Only rows on the `read` shelf are treated as finished. ISBNs are
exported as Excel-safe formulas (`="9780..."`) and unwrapped automatically, so matching resolves by
identifier where available.

```sh
storywell sync --source goodreads --file goodreads_library_export.csv
```

::: {.callout-note}
## What's validated
Parsing is validated against real exports (1,156 rows across three files, old and post-2022
layouts) with ~90% ISBN coverage. Many `read` rows have **no Date Read**, so those are marked read
without a finish date.
:::

### Kobo

- **Format:** ebook · **Flags:** `--file`

A Kobo e-reader stores its library in a SQLite database, `KoboReader.sqlite`, in the hidden
`.kobo` directory on the mounted device. Point Storywell at that file; books live in the `content`
table and the standard finished filter applies.

```sh
storywell sync --source kobo --file /Volumes/KOBOeReader/.kobo/KoboReader.sqlite
```

The schema is validated against a real device database (67-column `content` table); every column
read is present and the query runs without error.

## Newly added sources {#newly-added-sources}

These parse correctly against captured fixtures and follow the same proven patterns as the stable
sources, but haven't been exercised against a broad range of real exports/libraries yet. Run them
with `--dry-run` (sync) first and eyeball the match plan.

### Literal

- **Format:** mixed · **Flags:** `--token`

Reads your finished shelf from [Literal](https://literal.club) over its GraphQL API — a close cousin
of the Hardcover source, with cleaner data (ISBNs, ratings, and reviews come back directly). Log in
once to obtain a bearer token and pass it with `--token`, or set `LITERAL_TOKEN`. Books with Literal's
`FINISHED` status are marked read; finish dates are fetched per book.

```sh
export LITERAL_TOKEN="..."
storywell sync --source literal
```

### Apple Books

- **Format:** ebook · **Flags:** `--file` (optional) · **macOS only**

Mirrors the Kobo pattern: Apple Books keeps its library in an on-device SQLite database
(`BKLibrary*.sqlite`) under `~/Library/Containers/com.apple.iBooksX/`. Storywell finds it
automatically — pass `--file` only to point at a specific database. A book counts as finished when
Apple's finished flag is set or its reading progress clears the threshold; the database is opened
read-only. There are **no ISBNs** in this database, so matching is title/author based.

```sh
storywell sync --source applebooks
```

### Calibre

- **Format:** mixed · **Flags:** `--file`, `--read-column`

Reads your local [Calibre](https://calibre-ebook.com) library `metadata.db`. Calibre has **no
built-in read field**, so it needs `--read-column LABEL` naming the custom column you use to track
read status (a Yes/No, rating, or text column); a book counts as finished when that column is truthy.
ISBNs come from Calibre's `identifiers` table. Point `--file` at the library folder or the
`metadata.db` inside it; the database is opened read-only.

```sh
storywell sync --source calibre --file ~/Calibre\ Library --read-column "Read"
```

### Bookwyrm

- **Format:** mixed · **Flags:** `--file`

[Bookwyrm](https://joinbookwyrm.com) is a federated Goodreads alternative whose CSV export
(**Settings → Export**) is the richest of any file source — it carries shelf status, start/finish
dates, ratings, reviews, and both ISBNs. The `read` shelf is marked read with its finish date;
`currently-reading` and `to-read` rows are routed to their matching StoryGraph shelves.

```sh
storywell sync --source bookwyrm --file bookwyrm-export.csv
```

### LibraryThing

- **Format:** mixed · **Flags:** `--file`, `--shelf`, `--as-read`, `--read-date`, `--collection`

LibraryThing is a **catalogue, not a read-status tracker** — a typical export lists every book in
your library with no read flag and no Date Read. So Storywell reports the catalogue and lets you
decide which StoryGraph shelf each book lands on (see [shelf routing](#shelf-routing)):

- default: only books LibraryThing actually flags read (a "Read"-style collection or a real Date
  Read) count — for a pure catalogue that is usually none;
- `--shelf read`: route every catalogued book to **read** (the modern spelling of the legacy
  `--as-read`);
- `--shelf to-read` / `currently-reading` / `did-not-finish`: route the whole catalogue to that
  shelf instead — books LibraryThing already flags read still go to **read** (a finished signal
  always wins);
- `--read-date`: stamp today as a placeholder finish date on read books with no Date Read;
- `--collection NAME`: only import books in that collection (repeatable; omit for the whole
  catalogue).

```sh
# route a "Wishlist" collection to your StoryGraph to-read shelf
storywell sync --source librarything --file librarything_export.tsv \
  --collection "Wishlist" --shelf to-read
```

Both the TAB-delimited CSV and the `.json` export are accepted (JSON is preferred — its
`originaltitle` matches StoryGraph better).

### Libby / OverDrive

- **Format:** mixed · **Flags:** `--file`, `--shelf` (required)

Libby and OverDrive can export your borrowing history — the Libby **Timeline → Export → Spreadsheet**
CSV, or the OverDrive website **History** export. This is *borrow* activity, not reading status: no
finished flag, no finish date, no ISBN. Storywell therefore never claims a borrowed book was read —
you must opt the borrow list onto a shelf with `--shelf` (typically `to-read`), or nothing syncs.

```sh
storywell sync --source libby --file libbytimeline-activities.csv --shelf to-read
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Use the raw export
Export the **raw** Libby timeline, not Libby's "share to Goodreads" format — they have different
columns. Validated against a captured raw export; the schema is undocumented, so check a `--dry-run`.
:::

### Kindle

- **Format:** ebook · **Flags:** `--file`

Amazon has no live API, but its privacy portal does: **Request My Data → Kindle** emails you a ZIP
(it can take days to weeks to arrive) containing `Kindle.KindleDocs.DocumentMetadata.csv` and
per-session `Kindle.Devices.ReadingSession.csv` files. Point `--file` at the unzipped export folder.
The export has **no finished flag**, so Storywell infers "finished" heuristically from your reading
sessions — treat it as best-effort and always review a `--dry-run`. It keys on ASIN (no ISBN), so
matching is title/author based.

```sh
storywell sync --source kindle --file ~/Downloads/Kindle-export --dry-run
```

### Hardcover

- **Format:** mixed · **Flags:** `--token`

Reads your shelf over [Hardcover](https://hardcover.app)'s GraphQL API. Get a personal token at
[hardcover.app/account/api](https://hardcover.app/account/api) and pass it with `--token`, or set
`HARDCOVER_TOKEN`.

```sh
export HARDCOVER_TOKEN="hc_..."
storywell sync --source hardcover
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Experimental
The query and response mapping were verified against Hardcover's official GraphQL schema and field
access is defensive, but it has **not been run against a live token**, and "finished" relies on the
documented `status_id == 3` ("Read") mapping. Verify a `--dry-run` before trusting a write.
:::

## Shelf routing {#shelf-routing}

Most sources prove a book was *finished* and send it to your **read** shelf. Catalogue and borrow
sources (LibraryThing, Libby) carry no finished signal — so Storywell never marks their books read by
default. Instead you route them with `--shelf`:

- `--shelf to-read` / `currently-reading` / `did-not-finish` files the source's books on that shelf;
- a real finished signal always wins — a book the source *does* flag read still goes to **read**;
- read-tracker sources (Audible, Goodreads, Kobo, Hardcover, Literal, Apple Books, Calibre, Bookwyrm)
  stay read-only and ignore `--shelf` for already-finished books, so you can't accidentally flood a
  shelf.

This is why a borrow source like Libby requires `--shelf`: without it there is no signal to act on,
so nothing syncs.

## Services Storywell doesn't support — and why {#unsupported}

Storywell can add almost any service that exposes your data somehow — an export file, an on-device
database, or an API. The hard requirement is a **data path**: with no way to get your reading data
out, there is nothing to read. A second question is whether that data proves you *finished* a book;
when it only proves a *borrow*, *purchase*, or *ownership*, Storywell can still file those books on a
shelf via `--shelf`, but it never silently claims you read them.

None of the services below is an architecture limitation — each would be reconsidered the moment the
vendor ships an export or API with reading data.

### Being evaluated

- **Google Play Books** — the official Books API exposes a "Have read" shelf with ISBNs
  (`mylibrary/bookshelves`), which looks promising. It hinges on one unconfirmed question: whether the
  app's *Mark as finished* actually writes to that API shelf. (The Google Takeout export only contains
  highlight annotations — no reading status — so that path is a dead end.)
- **Spotify audiobooks** — the Web API exposes a per-chapter `resume_point.fully_played` completion
  flag under the `user-read-playback-position` scope. It hinges on whether that flag is reliable for
  audiobooks (it is known to be stale for podcasts) and on stamping a finish date at sync time. The
  account data download contains no audiobook listening data.

### No data path

No official export or public API, so there is nothing to read without reverse-engineering a private
app — brittle, and against their terms:

- **Storytel**, **BookBeat**, **Nextory** — subscription audiobook services.
- **Libro.fm** — you own the audiobooks, but listening progress lives only in the app.
- **Scribd / Everand** and **Nook (B&N)** — no export, no API.

### Borrow data only, with no export

- **Hoopla** and **Sora** — library apps whose activity is borrow-based and, unlike Libby/OverDrive,
  expose no retrievable export. If one appears, they'd slot in like Libby — routed to a shelf with
  `--shelf`.
